response.sql: SELECT player_id, death_country, award_count, award_count * 1.0 / SUM(award_count) OVER (PARTITION BY death_country) AS share FROM (SELECT ma.player_id AS player_id, p.death_country AS death_country, COUNT(*) AS award_count FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id WHERE p.death_country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ma.player_id, p.death_country) t ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST, player_id LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: player.player_id is unique, so the inner join does not duplicate manager_award rows.

The share's denominator is the sum of award rows across all managers with the same death_country, where the blank country is its own group. The denominator is computed only over managers who matched a player record and have a non-NULL death country.
Ties in share are broken by player_id, which the request does not specify, so the top 10 is deterministic.
